correctness.rationale: For every odd 5<=m<n, elementary 4-cycle squares force the root stabilizer to be precisely independent coordinate reflections. The stable refinement partition determines all root-to-vertex walk counts. Odd-factor unique coordinate geodesics give d=a+b and g=binomial(d,a). A lift to the integer square grid shows the first opposite-parity walk has length L=min(m-a+b,n+a-b); all other parity-flipping lifts are no shorter. Equality of d and g forces either identical profiles or coordinate swaps; with m<n, L strictly distinguishes every allowed nontrivial swap. Rooted orbits coincide with these ordered profiles, proving exact equality. The maximum first opposite-parity length is at most (m+n)/2, so round (m+n)/2 suffices. Literal 1-WL, BFS/parity-BFS, arithmetic injectivity and rooted automorphism programs were actually replayed successfully. Finite checks do not stand in for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an explicit all-parameter stable-orbit classification for a natural two-parameter family of four-regular rooted graph products, with exact class counts and a useful uniform diameter-plus-one refinement guarantee. The underlying mathematical obstruction is not an arbitrary numerical variation: when the factor lengths differ, automorphisms cannot swap factors but shortest-path multiplicities still cannot tell swapped distance profiles apart. The first parity-breaking winding time is a new structural certificate resolving precisely that obstruction. The conclusion is not reducible to an isolated experiment, a change of labels, or the previously known equal-factor case.
